studyPages.body:
WHY REPRODUCTION MATTERS
====

WHAT YOU WILL LEARN
----
• Say what why reproduction matters means in plain words.
• Use one real Kenyan example to show why reproduction matters.
• Correct one common mistake about why reproduction matters.

INTRODUCTION
----
Quick question: how would you explain Why Reproduction Matters — Continuity of human life age-appropriate to a classmate in one minute? Anchor answer: Continuity of human life age-appropriate. Clue from real life: 2.3 Reproduction in Human Beings. Check every example on this page against that anchor.

MAIN NOTES
----
• 2.3 Reproduction in Human Beings.
• Menstrual cycle consists of natural changes that occur to the body of a female human being every month in preparatio to pregnancy.
• A menstrual cycle lasts between 28-35 days. However, this can vary between female and from one cycle to the next. The cycle depends on hormones.
• Hormones are chemical messengers in the body.
• They direct the body on what to do and when to do it.
• The menstrual cycle is a process controlled by hormones in the female body.  The menstrual cycle is divided in to the following phases:.
• Bleeding from the vagina begins. This is caused by the loss of the lining of the uterus.

----

studyPages.title: Menstruation Explained
studyPages.body:
MENSTRUATION EXPLAINED
====

WHAT YOU WILL LEARN
----
• Say what menstruation explained means in plain words.
• Use one real Kenyan example to show menstruation explained.
• Correct one common mistake about menstruation explained.

INTRODUCTION
----
Each month, if pregnancy has not begun, the thickened lining of the uterus is shed as menstrual blood. That process is menstruation, often called periods. It is a normal biological event controlled by hormones, not a reason for shame.

MAIN NOTES
----
• This is called menstruation or monthly periods.
• If you are overweight, losing weight might help to make your periods regular.
• However, though common, you should see a doctor.  Heavy periods can be a sign of a health problem.
• Most women experience menstrual cramps before or during their period at some point in their lives.
• If you are underweight, slow and steady weight gain may help to regulate your menstrual circle.
• Bleeding is considered heavy if it interferes with normal activities.
• However, if the cramps are painful and persistent, you should see a doctor.

OVULATION EXPLAINED
====

WHAT YOU WILL LEARN
----
• Say what ovulation explained means in plain words.
• Use one real Kenyan example to show ovulation explained.
• Correct one common mistake about ovulation explained.

INTRODUCTION
----
Fertilization is the fusion of a sperm with an ovum in the oviduct (also called the fallopian tube.). That single observation is enough to unlock Ovulation Explained — Release of ovum. Also notice: Few sperms that reach the ovum try to penetrate it. Put simply, you are learning why that happens and how to say it accurately in an exam.

MAIN NOTES
----
• Fertilization is the fusion of a sperm with an ovum in the oviduct (also called the fallopian tube.).
• Few sperms that reach the ovum try to penetrate it.
• Only one sperm penetrates the ovum.
• When the sperm penetrates the ovum, the surface of the sperm fuses with the nucleus of the ovum to form a zygote.
• This is called menstruation or monthly periods.
